headline: Seven hours in, nothing meets the Marvel's Spider-Man 2 bar yet; every piece is climbing round by round under blind critics. Traversal R8 (camera 4), city R5 (street level built), characters R3 (thugs being rebuilt), lighting R2 (night) in progress. 4K/60 not reached (best ≈41 fps at TSR 50%, contaminated).
target: Marvel's Spider-Man 2 quality at 3840×2160 output, 60 fps, measured during real gameplay on the Mac Studio M3 Ultra.

critic.gap: Swings are flat: the hero holds one height down a rail-like corridor. Each swing must drop 2–4 storeys above the street and rise past the anchor, with the camera following height (vanishing point moving ≥15% of frame).
critic.notes: Reference won all four A/B pairs. Secondary: released web sweeps across the lens; camera clips into the hero during wall-run; wall-run has a frozen pose then a T-pose; tricks fire on every release. Scores: arc 3, camera 3, web 3, moves 2, body 2.

critic.gap: Replace the fixed-offset camera with a lagged chase camera 4–6 m behind and 1–2 m above, letting the hero move ≥20% of frame height per swing, never closer than 2 m, never inside the hero or a wall.
critic.notes: Blind A/B: the reference won all five pairs; round 2 beat round 1 by ~1 point. Secondary: 1.5–2 s rope-less glides between swings; anchors never visible; wall-run filmed straight at the wall and ends in a T-pose; hero smear at b 3.2 s.

critic.gap: Replace the grey ground plane at the city edge with city to the horizon, the Hudson and East rivers, a far shore and a haze band.
critic.notes: Reference won all 8 A/B pairs. Secondary: Times Square billboards black, jagged white artifact on the S3 roof, blank storefronts and an untextured cylinder in S1, long flat walls without cornices or fire escapes.

critic.gap: The air phase is dead: a rigid T-pose between release and the next attach, repeating every cycle. Needs a varied tuck/flip/extend/reach sequence and camera pitch that puts the hero against the sky at the top of the arc.
critic.notes: Camera passed its numeric checks (≥6 m from the hero, never in geometry) but still reads as locked behind. Rounds 1–3 scores barely moved: the placeholder body is the ceiling. Also found the A/B packs were identifiable by file hash; packs are now re-encoded.

critic.gap: Replace all foliage: leaf-cluster trees with alpha leaves, green albedo, light passing through; Central Park as a green canopy mass with paths.
critic.notes: Improving: skyline 2→4, Manhattan 2→4, facades 4→5; round 2 perch rated ~3 points better than round 1. Secondary: flat storefronts, blue-tinted far shore with white quays, untextured water tower, no hydrants/fire escapes, identical glowing windows.

critic.gap: Chase camera 4–5 m behind and 1–1.5 m above, pitched 10–20° down; hero ≥160 px tall at 1080p in ≥90% of frames; anchor and sky visible at each attach.
critic.notes: Up from round 3: body 2→4, arc 3→4, moves 2→3. The builder's telemetry claimed the hero filled 25% of frame height; pixels show 4–6%. Secondary: 1.2–1.5 s rope-less drifts; wall-run camera faces the wall; no landing crouch; torso flat against the rope at the arc bottom.

critic.gap: Wall-run: camera 3–5 m behind/below pitched 20–35° up the facade with the roof edge in frame; hero head-up with alternating hand/foot cycle at 2–3 steps/s; stays in frame through the top-out.
critic.notes: Up: arc 4→5, web 4→5, moves 3→4. Down: body 4→3 (one-frame pose pops on release, white unshaded suit at clip starts). Hero leaves frame during zip and wall top-out.

critic.gap: Dark reflective window glass with recessed frames and varied interiors; storefronts with visible interiors. Test: ≤10% of window pixels above 80% brightness in daylight crops.
critic.notes: Foliage fixed: round 3 beat round 2 on both street and park views. Critic flagged that upstream Times Square ads include Marvel/real-game brands (Oscorp, Osborn, Roxxon, Daily Bugle, Frosted Halos, Botanica); the Unreal port now excludes those cells. The browser build's atlas is upstream and unchanged.

critic.gap: Fix the brute's material/texture assignment so it reads as one heavy-set street criminal: solid clothes, no skin through them, lit readable head.
critic.notes: 39 assets evaluated individually on moving clips (21 keep, 13 refine, 5 replace). Secondary: civilians slide in a frozen pose; white crack artifacts on two citizens; hero lenses flat decals, web lines painted not raised, weave too coarse; hero run upright with no lean; AI suits walk in lockstep.

critic.gap: Swing cadence: attach→release 1.2–1.8 s, next web within 0.5 s, no web-less fall >0.6 s; ≥7 attaches in 12 s.
critic.notes: Best round yet: every axis 4–5; the new wall-run (head-up alternating climb, camera looking up the facade, flip top-out) rated ~2 points better than round 5. Deep drops from round 2 lengthened swings; round 7 keeps depth but adds speed.

critic.gap: Build street level: recessed storefronts with frames and interiors, awnings with original signs, piers and cornices, fire escapes, sidewalk slab joints, a hydrant/trash can/newspaper box/tree pit every ~20 m.
critic.notes: Windows fixed (interior atlas was sampled 2–4 mips too coarse at 50–73% internal resolution); round 4 beat round 3 in both version pairs. Critic flagged that reference HUD/logos made the blind test obvious: packs are now centre-cropped. Two ads (COLTEX/COLEX) too close to a real-game brand are being excluded.

critic.gap: Rebuild thug and brute to civilian quality: modelled heads/eyes, five-finger hands, folded clothes, real shoes; brute ≥1.3× thug shoulder width, upright heavy walk.
critic.notes: Brute texture fix confirmed (+~2 on enemies vs round 1). Critic also noted the hero's classic suit (white spider emblem, white cuffs, red leg stripes) closely resembles a licensed game suit design; flagged for the owner, not changed.

critic.gap: Night street lighting and exposure: lamp pools every 25–30 m, storefront spill, car lights, lifted ambient; night_S1 mean ≥35/255 with ≤3% of pixels <10/255; hero ≥40/255 in every night-swing frame.
critic.notes: Golden-hour haze from above works. Secondary: no warmth at street level at golden hour, a green lens ghost, 4.7% blown pixels at sunset, glass going black mid-swing, midday horizon darker than the sky.

critic.gap: Facade clearance and occlusion: keep ≥3 m wall clearance at the arc bottom, camera ≥1.5 m from facades; no facade >30% of frame in the problem spans.
critic.notes: Cadence targets met (7 attaches in 12 s, 1.1–1.75 s swings, rope on screen 81%); round 7 beat round 6 in both version pairs. Orchestrator check: the critic's '6–8% hero height' was wrong (frames show ~17%, matching telemetry); the wall-hugging at 14.5 s and the whole-frame blur are real and are the next gap.

critic.gap: Far skyline: window grids and material on every building past the first two rows; warm-neutral far shore; dark embankment with piers instead of a white strip; water reflecting the shore.
critic.notes: Street level built: 2,225 storefront bays with frames/awnings/original names, 616 fire escapes, street furniture every ~20 m; street dressing 3→4. More IP to exclude: 'HAUTE UNLIMITED' (real-game ad) and real-place evocations (Hotel Astor, Madison arena, L'Oréal-like).

critic.gap: Camera yaws toward the anchor and rolls with the arc; hero alternates 30–70% of frame width; arc low point varies ≥1 storey; keep facade clearance.
critic.notes: Wall-hugging fixed (nearest facade ~1 m → ≥13 m); round 8 beat round 7 in both version pairs; camera 3→4. Now too centred and repetitive.

gaps: 60 fps at 4K is not reached yet: best Unreal run ≈41 fps at TSR 50% (1080p internal); clean numbers need an idle GPU (other agents' Unreal runs hold it at 40–100%).
Unreal port has only a gray-box test map and a capsule character so far.
Default 4K output renders internally at 1920×1080 (50 %, TSR upscale); native 100 % is available via r.ScreenPercentage 100.

Owner decision: the browser build's upstream ad atlas (ts_ads.webp) shows Marvel-universe brands (Oscorp, Re-Elect Osborn, Roxxon, Daily Bugle) and likely real-game brands; the Unreal port excludes them, the browser build still shows them.
GitHub LFS budget exhausted: the 43 reference clips are local-only; refs/tools/regenerate_clips.sh rebuilds them anywhere.

Browser build bugs from the baseline playtest: camera top-down under tree canopy, camera inside hero, suit shader 17/16 texture units (~90 warnings/s), hero blocked by parked cars, Gemini/Qwen back logos, crowd clusters in lockstep, dark night street.

Owner decision: the default hero suit (upstream spiderman.glb) closely resembles a licensed game suit design (white spider emblem, white cuffs, red leg stripes). The AI-logo suits are original alternatives.

log.text: UE 5.8.3 installed; WebHomage project up with the official MCP on port 8765; spawn/remove round-trip verified.
Ownership contract NIGHT1.md committed; five agents launched (F1, F2, F3, P1, P2).
All six agents hit the weekly usage limit and stopped mid-round; nothing lost (uncommitted work kept in each worktree).
Limit reset. Resumed F1, F2, P1. Concurrency capped at three agents.
F1 merged: C++ module, mouse-safe controller (Escape always releases), Lumen + HW ray tracing on Metal SM6, offscreen 4K capture + 60 fps video.
Public fork refuses Git LFS uploads, so Unreal content is now rebuilt from committed scripts; binary snapshots go to the private repo webhomage-unreal-content.
P3 traversal + camera started (C++ port of traversal.js/camera.js with scripted input replays).
P3 round 1 merged; critic verdict FAILS TARGET; builder sent back on the flat-swing gap.
P3 round 2 merged (drop test passes); critic: FAILS TARGET, camera now the biggest gap.
P1 city round 1 merged (234 GLBs, 172 tile actors, 11k prop instances, facade shader ported to HLSL); critic FAILS; round 2 on horizon/rivers/haze.
Traversal R3 critic FAILS again; diagnosed a stall on the placeholder body; P3 now ports the browser animator onto the real hero. P2 characters resumed.
Traversal R4 merged: real hero with C++ animator; first real score gains; round 5 fixes camera framing using pixel-based measurement.
Correction: log times between 07:15 and 09:06 were earlier written 1–3 h late from estimates; fixed from commit timestamps.
The Claude Code session restarted and interrupted all agents. Each agent's unfinished work was committed as WIP and pushed; orphaned Unreal editors stopped; the merged foundation worktree torn down.

Blocker: the GitHub account's Git LFS budget is exhausted, so reference clips and Unreal binary snapshots can't be pushed anywhere. Unreal content is script-generated only; reference clips stay local on the Studio. Agents P1, P2, P3 resumed.
Owner: Sonnet 5.5 is the default subagent model (extra-high thinking); Opus 5.5 only for critics, deep engineering, integration. Rule landed in global AGENTS.md (main) and memory.
Started Sonnet 5.5 xhigh builders: P4 Look/lighting/4K perf round 1, F3 browser baseline finish, F2 reference index.
Traversal R5 merged; critic FAILS with gains on arc/web/moves; next gap = wall-run. Traversal builder hands off to a fresh Opus agent (context limit).
City R3 merged (foliage); critic FAILS, next gap = window glass. City round 4 now on a Sonnet 5.5 builder. IP: Marvel/real-game brand ads excluded in the Unreal port.
F2 reference library done on Sonnet 5.5: INDEX (219 stills, 43 clips, each viewed), SOURCES, tested clip-regeneration script; ~70 manifest labels corrected.
Characters R1 merged; critic FAILS; round 2 on a Sonnet 5.5 builder (brute texture).
Traversal R6 merged: wall-run fixed (critic +2 on that sequence); still FAILS; round 7 targets swing cadence.
City R4 merged (window glass + IP exclusions); critic FAILS, facades/IQ up to 5; round 5 builds street level. A/B packs now centre-cropped to hide reference HUD.

F3 browser baseline done (Sonnet): build/tests pass, 32 4K stills, 9 clips, 10-bug playtest. P4 lighting round 1 done: 3 time-of-day presets over the real city; 4K ≈41 fps best at TSR 50% (contaminated); with critic.

Incidents: a lighting-agent cleanup command targeted the owner's Chrome profile (macOS blocked it; profile intact). The baseline agent misread an owner message and pushed an unrequested AGENTS.md branch + memory note; both removed. Agents now have hard delete/edit limits.
Characters R2 merged: brute fixed (+2 on enemies); still FAILS; round 3 rebuilds thug/brute from existing Tripo people (no paid generation).
Look R1 critic FAILS (night 2/10); round 2 on a fresh Sonnet builder with measurable night targets.
Traversal R7 merged: swing-rhythm targets met; critic FAILS (flat scores). Verified frames myself: critic's size claim wrong, facade clearance + blur real → round 8.
City R5 merged (street level); critic FAILS; round 6 = far skyline + more IP exclusions.
Traversal R8 merged (facade clearance fixed); critic FAILS; round 9 = weave inside a safe corridor + dynamic camera.
